caption: The drawing is done in black pencil or charcoal on a beige paper background and depicts a lidded vessel, likely a tureen, shown in a three-dimensional view within a rectangular frame. The vessel has a rounded, bulging body with a narrower base and a matching domed lid that features a small knob or finial on top. Two horizontal handles protrude symmetrically from each side of the body. There is shading on the vessel giving it an appearance of volume and light reflection, with darker areas suggesting depth and curvature. In the bottom right corner of the drawing, there is an inset technical sketch of the same vessel in a simple side elevation, showing measurements and the vessel's silhouette. The artist’s signature, "Charles Cullen," is written in cursive just below the main frame on the lower left side of the paper.
title: Pewter Sugar Bowl
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
